item.category: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
item.description: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Rajya Sabha Passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by Voice Vote Bill Covers Entire Spectrum of Unfair Means Beyond Question Paper Leaks: Dr. Jitendra Singh Dr. Jitendra Singh Highlights Reforms Already Implemented to Make Public Examinations More Transparent, Efficient and Candidate-Friendly Government committed to safeguarding interests of students and youth through robust legal framework and comprehensive examination reforms Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 10:44PM by PIB Delhi The…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Rajya Sabha Passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by Voice Vote
Bill Covers Entire Spectrum of Unfair Means Beyond Question Paper Leaks: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Highlights Reforms Already Implemented to Make Public Examinations More Transparent, Efficient and Candidate-Friendly
Government committed to safeguarding interests of students and youth through robust legal framework and comprehensive examination reforms
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 10:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Rajya Sabha today passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, as passed by the Lok Sabha, by voice vote. Replying to the discussion on the Bill, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the amendments would further strengthen the legal framework for preventing unfair means in public examinations while safeguarding the interests of students and youth.

The Minister said the Government is committed to ensuring that public examinations remain transparent, credible and merit-based so that the sincere efforts of students are protected. Emphasising that the legislation is not confined to question paper leaks alone, he said the Bill seeks to prevent the entire spectrum of unfair means in public examinations. He said the law comprehensively addresses offences ranging from leakage of question papers and answer keys, tampering with answer sheets and computer systems, manipulation of examination processes, creation of fake websites and admit cards, to organised attempts to facilitate unfair means in examinations. These provisions, he said, reflect the comprehensive nature of the legislation in addressing diverse forms of examination-related malpractice.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government had brought the Amendment Bill with humility and an open mind, welcoming constructive suggestions from Members to further strengthen the legislation. He said the issue of unfair means in public examinations concerns every parent, every family and every citizen of the country, as it directly impacts the aspirations of students and the nation's future human resource.

Highlighting the Government's efforts to strengthen the education ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the National Education Policy 2020 has brought transformational reforms by providing greater academic flexibility and expanding opportunities for students. He informed the House that the number of universities in the country has increased from 760 to 1,293, while higher education institutions have grown from 51,534 to 64,896.

Referring to reforms in medical education, the Minister said the number of AIIMS has increased from seven to twenty-two, medical colleges from 387 to 844, undergraduate medical seats from 51,300 to 1.39 lakh and postgraduate medical seats from 31,000 to 86,300, making quality medical education more accessible and affordable.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the Government's initiatives for expanding educational opportunities and employment. He said 400 Eklavya Model Residential Schools are now functional across the country. Referring to employment generation, he said Government appointments increased from 7.22 lakh during 2004–2014 to 10.96 lakh during 2014–2024. He also noted that the Government has cleared backlog vacancies and undertaken special promotion drives to improve career progression in public service.

The Minister said the Government has also encouraged entrepreneurship among youth through the Startup India initiative. He informed the House that the number of recognised startups has increased from around 350–400 at the launch of the initiative to nearly 2.4 lakh today, making India the world's third-largest startup ecosystem. He also noted significant growth in innovation, research and intellectual property generation, with India now ranking among the leading countries in PhD output and patent filings.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 covers examinations conducted by major recruitment agencies, including the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) and the National Testing Agency (NTA). Highlighting reforms already introduced in examination systems, he said interviews have been abolished for specified government recruitments, online application systems and candidate-friendly examination processes have been introduced, provisional answer keys have enhanced transparency and cyber security measures have been strengthened. He further informed the House that the average recruitment cycle in the Staff Selection Commission has been reduced from nine months and eight days to eight months and twenty-four days. Referring to the Pratibha Setu initiative, he said the portal has been created to connect meritorious civil services candidates with prospective employers and that 335 private companies have already registered on the platform.

The Minister informed the House that implementation of the recommendations of the high-level expert committee constituted to strengthen the public examination ecosystem is progressing steadily. He said 35 of the committee's 46 recommendations have already been implemented, including Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, AI-enabled face authentication, multi-layer frisking, CCTV surveillance, signal jammers, State and district coordination committees, grievance redressal mechanisms and restructuring of the National Testing Agency.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said strengthening the integrity of public examinations requires the collective participation of Government, educational institutions, parents, students and society at large. Reiterating that the Government remains open to constructive suggestions from all stakeholders, he said the Government will continue to strengthen the public examination system to ensure that it remains fair, transparent, credible and free from unfair means while safeguarding the aspirations of millions of students and job aspirants.

 

 

 

 

*****

Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 9:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the establishment of a Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the presence of Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. The MoU marks a significant milestone in strengthening India’s domestic telecom manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector.

The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is envisaged as an integrated 350-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster, designed to provide world-class infrastructure and a conducive ecosystem for telecom and electronics manufacturing, research and development, innovation and allied activities. The initiative is aimed at positioning Gwalior as a premier industrial and technology hub in Central India and strengthening India’s position as a global telecom manufacturing and innovation hub.

The signing of the MoU will pave the way for the establishment of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for the TMZ, with 51 per cent equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49 per cent from the Department of Telecommunications.

The Central Government is providing 100 per cent funding support for Phase-I, with an allocation of ₹493 crore for development of core infrastructure. The Government of Madhya Pradesh, in turn, has extended significant support for the project, including approximately 170 acres of land free of cost.

Under the special policy package extended by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, 100 acres in the SADA region and 70 acres in the Gwalior IT Park have been allocated free of cost, with a combined value of approximately ₹596 crore. Additional land will be made available at a nominal premium of ₹1 and a fixed lease rent of ₹1 per square metre per annum for 30 years. Units established in the TMZ will also benefit from reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges, power tariff rebates and other fiscal incentives.

The policy package provides substantial support to investors and manufacturers, including 50 per cent capital subsidy on Eligible Fixed Capital Investment (EFCI), subject to a maximum of ₹200 crore, along with employment generation assistance of ₹5,000 per month per employee for five years for eligible mega projects. Skill development support of up to ₹13,000 per new employee will also be available, subject to applicable conditions.

To promote exports, eligible units will receive a 50 per cent freight subsidy on finished goods transported to seaports or air cargo facilities, subject to prescribed limits. The package also provides incentives for research and development, including reimbursement support for standalone R&D units and 100 per cent reimbursement of expenses incurred for filing patents, copyrights and trademarks, within specified limits.

The TMZ is expected to serve as a major investment catalyst, with initial commitments of approximately ₹5,000 crore for Phase-I and projected total investments of ₹12,000–15,000 crore over time. The project is expected to generate approximately 14,000 direct skilled jobs, including around 3,500 jobs in Phase-I, besides creating tens of thousands of indirect employment opportunities.

Leading telecom and electronics companies, including Dixon Technologies, HFCL, Tejas Networks, VVDN and Syrma SGS, are among the industry players anchoring the proposed zone.

The TMZ is envisaged to bring together the entire telecom value chain, ranging from mobile devices and optical fibre to advanced semiconductor technologies and next-generation 5G/6G research and development. Dedicated R&D centres, common testing laboratories and certification facilities will support the development and validation of indigenous telecom technologies and products in accordance with global standards.

The initiative will also create synergies with key national programmes, including the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) and Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF). By strengthening domestic manufacturing of critical telecom equipment such as routers, antennas, optical fibre and chips, the TMZ will contribute towards reducing import dependence, promoting exports, strengthening domestic supply chains and enhancing telecom security.

Expressing his view, Shri Jyotiraditya Madhavrao Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region said, “India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone will be established in Gwalior, the heart of the country, and will accelerate Madhya Pradesh’s growth trajectory.” He said this is a historic milestone in realizing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, Digital India and Viksit Bharat 2047 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The project will strengthen India’s position on the global telecom manufacturing map. He added that under the leadership of Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, Madhya Pradesh is progressing rapidly towards development and self-reliance, and the Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a clear reflection of that vision.

The Union Minister also added, “India must now move beyond being a telecom service provider to becoming a telecom manufacturer, and that building a strong indigenous ecosystem is essential to achieving this goal. The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a major step in that direction.”

Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister, Madhya Pradesh highlighted the significance of TMZ in his state and said, “ The Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is the outcome of Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s sustained efforts and visionary leadership.” He highlighted the Shri Scindia family’s historic contribution to the development of Gwalior and said the project represents another important chapter in that journey.

The Chief Minister expressed confidence that the Telecom Manufacturing Zone would shape not only the industrial and technological future of Madhya Pradesh but also of the country. “What cannot be found anywhere else in India will now be available in Madhya Pradesh,” he said, adding that Gwalior is set to become a national hub for electronics and telecom manufacturing, attracting significant investment, employment and technological innovation.

Speaking on the development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development said, “It is a historic day for both Department of Telecommunications and Government of Madhya Pradesh for establishing first of its kind similar to a SEZ where you put everything from end to end whether it is research, manpower, design, testing and manufacturing in one area. We want to design, patents and intellectual property rights and globally competitive products and this manufacturing zone will help in achieving that.”

Following the MoU signing, an Investor Roundtable was held under the joint chairmanship of Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. The roundtable brought together representatives of telecom manufacturers and industry stakeholders from across the country to discuss investment opportunities, industry requirements and the potential of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior to strengthen India’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem. Various industry leaders applauded the initiative of the both Central and state governments and termed as a historic and best in the world offer and opportunity for the telecom manufacturers and stakeholders. At the end of the roundtable, a total of INR 3,500 crore investment and 14,000 job opportunities were committed by the industry towards the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

The establishment of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior represents a strategic step towards creating a globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem in India. By integrating manufacturing, R&D, common infrastructure, policy support and industry participation, the TMZ is expected to drive investments, create high-quality employment, boost exports, promote indigenous innovation and strengthen India’s telecom supply chain.

The signing of the MoU between the Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh marks the beginning of a new chapter in India’s journey towards becoming a global hub for telecom manufacturing and innovation.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Continues Educational Support for OBC Students Through Scholarships and Free Coaching Schemes Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class Education and Free Coaching Schemes Ensuring Greater Access to Quality Education for OBC Students Across the Country Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 9:27PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India continues to strengthen educational opportunities for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) through a comprehensive set of scholarship and coaching schemes aimed at improving access to…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Continues Educational Support for OBC Students Through Scholarships and Free Coaching Schemes
Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class Education and Free Coaching Schemes Ensuring Greater Access to Quality Education for OBC Students Across the Country
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 9:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen educational opportunities for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) through a comprehensive set of scholarship and coaching schemes aimed at improving access to quality education and enhancing their participation in higher education and competitive examinations. These initiatives are designed to provide financial assistance, academic support and equal opportunities to students from socially and educationally disadvantaged communities.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM, SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI, SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL, SHRI NILESH DNYANDEV LANKE, DR. SHIVAJI BANDAPPA KALGE in the Lok Sabha.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing a number of welfare schemes for OBC students, including the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs & Others, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs & Others, Top Class Education in Schools for OBCs & Others, Top Class Education in Colleges for OBCs & Others, and the Free Coaching Scheme for Scheduled Castes (SCs), OBCs and beneficiaries of the PM CARES Children Scheme.

Financial assistance under the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes is released to States and Union Territories based on Notional Allocation, enabling them to extend scholarship benefits to eligible students. Under the Top Class Education Schemes and the Free Coaching Scheme, financial assistance is transferred directly to eligible beneficiaries through the Aadhaar-enabled Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism, ensuring transparency and timely disbursal of benefits.

The Central Sector Scheme of Free Coaching seeks to enhance the competitiveness of students from disadvantaged communities by providing quality coaching for various competitive examinations conducted for recruitment to Government and private sector jobs, as well as for admission to reputed technical and professional higher educational institutions.

The scheme is currently being implemented through Dr. Ambedkar Centres of Excellence (DACE) established in 19 empanelled Central Universities, with 100 coaching seats earmarked in each university. In Maharashtra, Mahatma Gandhi Hindi Antarrashtriya Vishwavidyalaya, Wardha, has been empanelled under the scheme. In Madhya Pradesh, the scheme is being implemented through Indira Gandhi National Tribal University, Amarkantak, and Dr. Harisingh Gour Vishwavidyalaya, Sagar. At present, there is no empanelled Central University under the scheme in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

The Minister further informed that the revision of scholarship and coaching assistance under these schemes is undertaken periodically in consultation with all concerned stakeholders, ensuring that the schemes remain responsive to the educational needs of students while supporting the Government's vision of inclusive and equitable development.

The Government reiterated its commitment to ensuring that no deserving student is deprived of educational opportunities due to financial constraints. Through sustained investments in scholarships, quality coaching and direct financial assistance, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower OBC students with the knowledge, skills and opportunities required to participate effectively in the nation's social and economic progress.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Swachhata Pakhwada 2026: Ministry of MSME Reinforces Commitment to Cleanliness, Sustainability and Jan Bhagidari
Ministry of MSME Drives Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 with Tree Plantation Drives, Cleanliness Pledges, and Sustainable Practices Across India
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is observing Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16th  to 31st  July 2026 through a broad range of activities that underscore its commitment to environmental sustainability and the vision of Swachh Bharat. Organised across the Ministry's offices, attached and subordinate organisations, autonomous bodies and field formations, the campaign promotes waste reduction, resource conservation, tree plantation, cleanliness, eco-friendly practices and environmental awareness, while encouraging employees and stakeholders to adopt sustainable habits and contribute to building a cleaner, greener and more resilient India.

Shri Jitan Ram Majhi, Union Minister for MSME, Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME, and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME) participated in a plantation drive under the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative. The activity reflected the Ministry's commitment to promoting environmental conservation alongside the objectives of Swachhata Pakhwada, while reinforcing the message that cleanliness and a green environment go hand in hand. The plantation drive also encouraged greater environmental consciousness and public participation, highlighting the importance of collective efforts towards building a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

   

The campaign gathered significant momentum with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME). Officers and employees of the Ministry, along with officials from its attached and subordinate organisations, participated in the pledge-taking ceremony, reaffirming their collective resolve to uphold the ideals of cleanliness and contribute meaningfully to the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

 

Further strengthening the Swachhata Pakhwada campaign, Shri Vinamra Mishra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of MSME, addressed officers and representatives of the Ministry's attached organisations, subordinate offices and field formations during a 'Swachhata Talk' organised as part of the Pakhwada. Emphasising that cleanliness is not merely a periodic campaign but a shared civic responsibility, he urged all organisations to actively participate in the Swachhata Pakhwada by organising meaningful cleanliness drives, awareness programmes and sustainable initiatives within their offices as well as in the surrounding communities.

   

Throughout the Pakhwada, the Ministry is encouraging its attached, subordinate and field offices across the country to undertake a diverse range of activities, including cleanliness drives, plantation programmes, public awareness campaigns, record management and disposal, waste segregation, reduction of single-use plastics and other citizen-centric initiatives that foster sustainable practices and community participation.

 

The Ministry of MSME, through the successful conduct of Swachhata Pakhwada activities, reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of "Swachh Bharat – Swasth Bharat." The campaign served as a platform to encourage employees, stakeholders and citizens to adopt cleanliness as a way of life, strengthen environmental consciousness and work collectively towards a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

"Swachhata is not merely a campaign; it is a shared responsibility and a lasting commitment towards nation-building."

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DELIVERY OF SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL - ‘NIPUN’
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

‘Nipun’ the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV), built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited was delivered to the Indian Navy on 30 Jul 2026 at Visakhapatnam. The vessel has been designed and constructed in accordance with Classification Rules of the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS).

 ‘Nipun’ draws her name from Sanskrit signifying ‘one who is adept, capable, and well versed in a particular discipline’. True to the name, the ship is highly specialised and is capable of undertaking deep sea dive operations and rescue operations at sea.

The ship is installed with state-of-the-art Dive Equipment and has capability to undertake Deep Sea Saturation Diving. A side diving stage has also been provided for undertaking Diving Operations. The Remotely Operated Vehicles further enhance the ship’s operational capabilities by facilitating diver monitoring and salvage operations. In addition, the ship would also serve as the Mother Ship for the Deep Submergence Rescue Vessel (DSRV), to evacuate personnel in case of an emergency in a submarine.

Nipun’s delivery is yet another milestone in the Indian Navy’s quest for indigenous Shipbuilding upholding the Government’s vision of an ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ with nearly 75 percent Indigenous Content. The delivery marks a major step in bolstering the Indian Navy’s capabilities in the niche domain of Deep Sea Dive Operations.

item.category: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways India Expedites Maritime Capacity Expansion as Government Pushes Viksit Bharat 2047 Goals Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal urges ‘Faster Execution’, calls for 'Speed & Scale' to meet 2030 maritime targets Govt identifies Port Capacity, Shipbuilding and Digitisation emerge as key Growth Drivers Port expansion pipeline targets over 700 MTPA of Additional Capacity by 2030 Higher mechanisation, greater private participation to to reshape India's port Ecosystem by 2030 Shipbuilding output surges 41% as New Industrial Clusters position India for Global…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
India Expedites Maritime Capacity Expansion as Government Pushes Viksit Bharat 2047 Goals
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal urges ‘Faster Execution’, calls for 'Speed & Scale' to meet 2030 maritime targets
Govt identifies Port Capacity, Shipbuilding and Digitisation emerge as key Growth Drivers
Port expansion pipeline targets over 700 MTPA of Additional Capacity by 2030
Higher mechanisation, greater private participation to to reshape India's port Ecosystem by 2030
Shipbuilding output surges 41% as New Industrial Clusters position India for Global Manufacturing Growth
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

India is accelerating investments across ports, inland waterways and shipbuilding as the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) advances its roadmap towards Viksit Bharat 2047, with a sharp focus on capacity creation, private investment, digitisation and maritime manufacturing.

Chairing a high-level review of the Ministry's Viksit Bharat targets, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping & Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal directed officials to accelerate implementation of flagship projects while maintaining strict adherence to timelines. Sonowal urged officials across the Ministry, major ports and the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) to work with a unified approach to achieve India's long-term maritime ambitions.

The review comes as the Ministry reports significant progress across multiple performance indicators. India has consolidated its position as the world's largest ship recycling nation, while inland waterways cargo has already crossed 200 million tonnes, achieving the Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030 target several years ahead of schedule.

"These achievements demonstrate what India can accomplish when policy, execution and teamwork move together. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the maritime sector has emerged as one of the strongest pillars of India's economic transformation. We must continue to work with the same sense of purpose, uphold the Prime Minister's mantra of ‘Speed and Scale’, and ensure that every milestone under ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ is delivered on time," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Minister also called on officials to strengthen institutional resilience by incorporating lessons from global disruptions into future planning."The evolving geopolitical situation has shown that resilience is as important as growth. Every challenge offers an opportunity to build stronger systems, enhance capacity and prepare India for the future. Our planning must anticipate global uncertainties while keeping India's growth trajectory firmly on course," Sonowal said.

700 MTPA Capacity Addition by 2030

The Ministry is pursuing one of the country's largest maritime infrastructure expansion programmes, targeting more than 700 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of additional port capacity by 2030. Among the flagship projects are the Vadhavan Port, which will add 164 MTPA of capacity by 2030-31, the Tuticorin Outer Harbour project with 39 MTPA, and the Kandla Tuna Tekra Terminal, expected to contribute 33 MTPA by 2027-28.

Overall, the Ministry plans to create an additional 682 MTPA of capacity by 2030 through a combination of new infrastructure, mechanisation and private investment. This includes 306 MTPA at major ports, 193 MTPA at key non-major ports and another 183 MTPA through mechanisation, operational efficiency improvements, public-private partnerships and capacity augmentation at emerging non-major ports.

Mechanisation, PPP to Drive Efficiency

The Ministry aims to increase cargo handling mechanisation across ports from 76% in FY 2025-26 to 93% by 2030, significantly improving operational efficiency and reducing turnaround time. Private sector participation is also expected to expand substantially. Cargo handled through public-private partnership (PPP) projects is projected to rise from 44% in 2013-14 to 85% by 2030-31, reflecting the Government's continued emphasis on private capital and operational expertise in port development. The Ministry has also set a target of achieving 100% digitisation across the maritime sector by 2030, with integrated digital platforms expected to improve logistics efficiency, transparency and service delivery.

Shipbuilding Push Gains Momentum

India's shipbuilding sector also recorded strong momentum during the review period. Domestic shipbuilding output increased 41%, rising from 40,923 gross tonnes (GT) in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025. To support long-term manufacturing growth, the Government has granted in-principle approvals for greenfield shipbuilding clusters in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, each with a planned capacity of 1.2 million GT. Similar approvals for Maharashtra and Odisha are expected by August-September 2026.

A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding has also been signed with HD Hyundai-KSOE for developing a shipbuilding cluster in Tamil Nadu, while extending 100% financial support for common maritime infrastructure required for these industrial ecosystems. The review noted a sharp improvement in the value of vessels being built domestically. The average contract value per vessel has increased more than fivefold to ₹212 crore, compared with ₹41 crore previously, indicating India's growing capability to manufacture larger and technologically advanced ships.

The Union Minister underlined the Ministry's roadmap under Viksit Bharat 2047 to position India among the world's leading maritime economies by strengthening infrastructure, expanding logistics capacity, boosting domestic manufacturing and enhancing global competitiveness.

The…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
APEDA Facilitates First-Ever Sea Shipment of Value-Added Flavoured Makhana from Bihar to Canada
Value-Added Makhana Exports Boost Farmers' Returns by Over 50%, Strengthen Bihar's Global Footprint
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, facilitated the flag-off of the first-ever sea shipment of value-added flavoured Makhana (fox nuts) from Darbhanga, Bihar, to Canada on 29 July 2026. The milestone export marks a significant step in promoting Bihar's premium agricultural produce in global markets while expanding the state's basket of value-added agricultural exports.

The consignment, comprising 7 metric tonnes packed in two containers, was dispatched through Mundra Port to ZKV Foods, Canada. The flavoured Makhana was processed and packaged by Nutrivin Agro Private Limited in accordance with international quality and food safety standards, reflecting Bihar's growing capabilities in food processing, value addition and export-oriented manufacturing.

The flag-off ceremony was graced by APEDA Chairman, Shri Abhishek Dev, who appreciated the collective efforts of the exporter, processors, farmers, industry stakeholders and APEDA officials in facilitating the shipment. He said such collaborative initiatives are strengthening Bihar's agri-export ecosystem, promoting value-added agricultural products and expanding global market access for the state's unique produce.

The event was attended by Dr. Manoj Kumar, Scientist, ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga; Shri Loknath Thakur, District Agriculture Marketing Officer; senior officers of APEDA; and exporters and stakeholders associated with the Makhana value chain.

Makhana, popularly known as fox nuts, is one of Bihar's flagship agricultural products, with the state accounting for the largest share of India's production. Renowned for its nutritional value and premium quality, Bihar's Makhana has witnessed growing demand in international markets owing to increasing consumer preference for healthy and value-added food products. The export of flavoured Makhana is expected to further diversify export opportunities while enhancing the global recognition of this unique product.

The export of value-added flavoured Makhana has enabled associated Makhana farmers to realise over 50 per cent higher returns through value addition and improved access to international markets. It also demonstrates the potential of processing, branding and export-oriented value addition in enhancing the competitiveness of India's agricultural products while strengthening farmers' integration with global value chains.

APEDA has been consistently working to develop Bihar as a leading agri-export hub through capacity building, export infrastructure development, quality compliance, market linkages and value addition. It continues to work closely with State Governments, exporters, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), processors and other stakeholders to strengthen India's agri-export ecosystem through quality assurance, export facilitation and market development. The successful sea shipment of flavoured Makhana to Canada marks another important milestone in these efforts, creating sustainable income opportunities for farmers, processors and exporters while further enhancing the global presence of Bihar's premium agricultural products.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
UNION MINISTER OF JAL SHAKTI CHAIRS MEETING WITH CHIEF MINISTERS OF CHHATTISGARH AND ODISHA TO FACILITATE AN AMICABLE SETTLEMENT OF THE MAHANADI WATER DISPUTE
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Paatil, today chaired a meeting with Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, and Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Chief Minister of Odisha, to facilitate an amicable settlement of the Mahanadi Water Dispute. Senior officers of the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Central Water Commission (CWC), and the Governments of both the States also attended the meeting.

The meeting marks an important step in the ongoing efforts of the Government of India to facilitate an amicable settlement of the Mahanadi Water Dispute through dialogue, technical cooperation and cooperative federalism.

Over the past several years, extensive deliberations and efforts have been made at various levels regarding the sharing of the waters of the Mahanadi. Following the request of the State of Odisha, the Government of India constituted the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal (MWDT) on 12 March 2018 under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956. The Central Government also extended the tenure of the Tribunal to ensure that all parties were provided adequate opportunity to present their views.

Recently, the process has gained further momentum with both the States demonstrating their willingness to pursue an amicable settlement through mutual cooperation and technical consultations.

The meeting also took note of the progress made by the Joint Technical Committee, which has held number of meetings and achieved consensus on several technical issues. It also noted the constitution of the expanded Technical Committee under chairmanship of Chairman Central Water Commission and comprising representatives of the Governments of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, whose first meeting was held on 29 July 2026 to take forward the remaining technical consultations.

Welcoming the Chief Ministers, Shri C. R. Paatil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti observed that the Mahanadi is a lifeline for millions of people in both the States. He emphasized that dialogue, technical cooperation and mutual trust are the most effective means of achieving an equitable, sustainable and mutually acceptable solution.

The Union Minister acknowledged the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in bringing states together to resolve long standing water disputes. The Union Minister highlighted that recent milestones, including the signing of the Yamuna Water Project Agreement, the resolution of issues relating to the implementation of the Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal Award, and the consensus on the Modified Parbati–Kalisindh–Chambal (MPKC) Link Project, underscore that even the most complex inter-State water disputes can be resolved through sustained dialogue, cooperative federalism, and consensus-based decision-making.

Both the Chief Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to continue the ongoing technical consultations in a constructive spirit and appreciated the facilitation provided by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Central Water Commission.

Concluding the meeting, Shri C. R. Paatil reiterated that the objective is not merely to resolve the present dispute but to establish a long-term, equitable and sustainable framework for the management of the Mahanadi Basin. He expressed confidence that the continued constructive engagement between the two States would pave the way for a mutually acceptable and enduring settlement.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs CCS Meeting to review the situation in context of ongoing West Asia Conflict
PM calls for a unified and coordinated mechanism for regular monitoring of all developments to ensure expeditious implementation of measures safeguarding citizens' interests
PM asks to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families
Requirement for fertilizers for the ensuing Rabi season assessed; PM says that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers
PM says all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict
PM emphasises usage of renewable energy sources
Cabinet Secretary briefs about initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today chaired a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CSS) to review the situation in the context of ongoing West Asia conflict and measures taken by various Ministries and Departments. This was the 4th special CCS meeting on the issue.

Cabinet Secretary briefed the CCS about the present geo-political situation. He spoke about the initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products, including LNG/LPG and fertilizers. He said that sources for procurement of LPG have already been diversified and the overall stock and supply position of major petroleum products remain adequate. Availability of adequate crude oil has enabled Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) refineries to operate at utilisation levels exceeding 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products. Initiatives have also been taken to expand Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections which have resulted in substantial increase in PNG connections. The Government is also facilitating industrial substitution of LPG through expansion of the National Gas Grid, augmentation of LNG import and regasification infrastructure, expansion of City Gas Distribution networks, and time-bound pipeline and last-mile connectivity approvals under the Pipeline Infrastructure Order, 2026.

During the meeting, requirements for the fertilizers for the ensuing Rabi season was assessed and alternate sources of fertilizers were also discussed. Prime Minister said that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers.

The situation of Seafarers serving on domestic as well as foreign-flagged vessels in conflict zones was also deliberated. Prime Minister directed to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families.

Prime Minister said that all efforts must be made to safeguard the citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict.

Prime Minister said that in order to ensure energy independence, emphasis should be made on renewable energy sources including solar energy and other non-fossil-fuel based sources.

Prime Minister said that a whole of government approach be continued to be adopted to tackle the challenges arising due to the crisis. He said that a unified coordinated mechanism be put in place for regular monitoring of all the developments to ensure expeditious implementation of appropriate measures to safeguard the interests of the citizens.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Facts about Ethanol Blended Petrol: Separating Facts from Misconceptions
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Certain misleading claims regarding the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme have recently been circulated in the media and on social media. The following point-wise clarifications, based on scientific validation, extensive field experience and industry data, address these claims and present the factual position.

Claim 1: Vehicles manufactured before 2023 cannot run on E20 petrol.

  • E15-plus fuel has been in widespread use for over three and a half years, while E19-E20 fuel has been in use for over two and a half years.
  • During this period, no verified news of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending has emerged. Had ethanol blending been causing systemic damage to engines or fuel systems, such failures would have resulted in large-scale warranty claims, service campaigns and widespread consumer complaints, none of which have been reported.
  • Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil operating higher ethanol blends for decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained around 1.53% in 2013-14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after creating the necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework.

As seen from the table,the progression has been gradual:

 

 

Ethanol Supply Year

Average Blending(%)

2013-14

~1.53

2020-21

~8.1

2021-22

~10

2022-23

~12

2023-24

~14.6

2024-25

~19.2

2025-26 (Nov-June)

20
  • The Government has also considered the large-scale real-world operating experience. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles),
  • The Government's assessment is also based on manufacturer service data. A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2 wheeler company has reported similar field experience.
  • Further, the rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).
  • Material compatibility, engine calibration, drivability, durability, emissions, fuel systems and performance were scientifically evaluated before implementation. Manufacturers have continued to honour vehicle warranties, reflecting their confidence in the compatibility of the fuel.
  • One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion, while ARAI reaffirmed that E20-compatible vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers.
  • In addition, Oil Marketing Companies maintain strict fuel quality assurance through over 30,000 retail outlet inspections for adulteration and fuel quality verification, supported by directions to States to maintain zero tolerance towards fuel adulteration. Ethanol-blended petrol conforms to BIS specifications and undergoes quality checks throughout the supply chain.
  • Accordingly, the Government's statement that "no widespread issues" have been reported is based not on isolated instances but on the cumulative evidence of over 25 years of phased implementation, extensive scientific validation, continuous field experience across crores of vehicles, manufacturer service records, stakeholder consultations, and ongoing quality monitoring.
  • The Government examines claims circulated on social media in consultation with manufacturers and technical agencies. Many such claims have been found to be exaggerated, misleading or unsupported by technical evidence and no verified evidence of widespread engine damage due to ethanol blending has emerged.

Claim 2: Nearly 30 crore vehicles will become unusable.

E15+ blended petrol has already been in widespread use for more than three and a half years, while E19-E20 fuel has been in use for over two and a half years.

During this period:

  • More than 20 crore two-wheelers
  • More than 3 crore petrol cars have operated on these fuels without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending.

If E20 really rendered vehicles unusable, India would have witnessed millions of breakdowns, warranty claims and service campaigns. Nothing of that sort has occurred.

Claim 3: Automobile manufacturers have privately indicated that E20 is not desirable.

On 4 July 2026, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, along with the Ministry of Heavy Industries and the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, convened a joint press conference where senior executives from Toyota Kirloskar, Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto collectively addressed concerns regarding E20. Their position was unequivocal:

  • Toyota Kirloskar stated that E20 was introduced only after rigorous testing on older vehicles, describing ethanol as a clean, high-performance fuel that has been used globally for decades. It further emphasised that testing protocols are internationally standardised under UNECE norms and cannot be compromised.
  • Maruti Suzuki gave what it described as a "statement of confidence" to consumers. Based on 2.84 crore vehicles serviced in FY 2025-26, including more than 1.5 crore older vehicles that were not originally E20-certified, the company reported no E20-related corrosion, abnormal wear, or reduction in component life. It also clarified that the mileage impact is generally limited to 3–3.5%, and that everyday factors such as tyre pressure, driving style, maintenance and traffic have a much larger influence on fuel economy.
  • Hero MotoCorp, one of the world's largest two-wheeler manufacturers, stated that analysis of its extensive service data found no higher incidence of damage in vehicles operating on E20 compared to earlier fuels.
  • Hyundai, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto also participated in the same press conference and collectively reaffirmed the industry's confidence in the E20 programme. The panel concluded by reiterating its commitment to the programme and to addressing consumer concerns transparently.

Claim 4: Older vehicles are at risk.

A leading automobile manufacturer serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26.

Among them were approximately 1.5 crore vehicles that were never originally certified as E20-compatible.

Despite this,

  • no abnormal corrosion,
  • no abnormal wear,
  • no reduction in component life was attributed to E20 fuel.

A leading two-wheeler manufacturer has reported similar field experience, while another OEM tracked 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles over an extended period and found no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion.

Claim 5: Mileage will collapse.

Government studies and automobile manufacturers have consistently explained that fuel efficiency depends on multiple factors, including:

  • driving habits,
  • traffic conditions,
  • vehicle maintenance,
  • tyre pressure,
  • air-conditioner usage.

For certain older E10-designed vehicles, any reduction in fuel economy is generally limited to about 3-5%, not the exaggerated figures being circulated.

At the same time, E20 provides:

  • higher octane rating, superior anti-knock characteristics,
  • cleaner combustion, smoother engine performance,
  • better acceleration and ride quality.

Claim 6: Manufacturers are being forced to support E20.

Had automobile manufacturers not been satisfied with the scientific validation, they would neither

  • have certified E20-compatible vehicles,
  • nor continued to honour warranty obligations.

Manufacturers continue to honour warranties for vehicles operating on specification-compliant E20 fuel because they have confidence in the extensive testing that preceded the rollout.

Claim 7: Automobile companies are under Government pressure to hide the truth about E20.

  • India's automobile manufacturers are independent listed companies with legal and regulatory obligations to their customers.
  • They cannot conceal widespread vehicle defects without exposing themselves to warranty claims, product liability, regulatory action and serious reputational damage.
  • Manufacturers continue to honour warranties for E20-compatible vehicles, something they would not do if they believed E20 was causing systemic engine damage. Warranty decisions are based on engineering validation and field experience and not political considerations.
  • The industry's position has also been expressed publicly and transparently. On 4 July 2026, senior executives from Toyota Kirloskar, Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto jointly addressed the media. They reaffirmed that E20 was introduced only after rigorous testing and extensive validation.

Their statements were backed by real-world service data:

  • Maruti Suzuki analysed 2.84 crore vehicles serviced in FY 2025-26, including over 1.5 crore older vehicles, and found no E20-related corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life.
  • Hero MotoCorp reported that its extensive service data showed no higher incidence of vehicle damage in two-wheelers operating on E20.
  • Toyota Kirloskar stated that E20 was introduced only after rigorous testing on older vehicles, following internationally recognised testing protocols under UNECE standards.

*****

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, along with President Smt. Droupadi Murmu, interacts with the Manjhi-Chalaki, the leading representatives of Bastar’s social traditions, and winners of Bastar Pandum today.

In a post on X, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said, “Today, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, I, along with Hon’ble President Smt. item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Over 25.85 Lakh Scheduled Caste Students in Tamil Nadu Benefitted from Central Scholarship Schemes in Three Years Government Strengthens Educational Access, Social Protection and Economic Empowerment Through Scholarships, PM-AJAY, PM-YASASVI and Other Welfare Initiatives Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government has reiterated its commitment to advancing educational opportunities, strengthening social protection and promoting economic empowerment for vulnerable communities in Tamil Nadu through a wide…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Over 25.85 Lakh Scheduled Caste Students in Tamil Nadu Benefitted from Central Scholarship Schemes in Three Years
Government Strengthens Educational Access, Social Protection and Economic Empowerment Through Scholarships, PM-AJAY, PM-YASASVI and Other Welfare Initiatives
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reiterated its commitment to advancing educational opportunities, strengthening social protection and promoting economic empowerment for vulnerable communities in Tamil Nadu through a wide range of welfare programmes being implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The initiatives cover Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Economically Backward Classes, Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, senior citizens, sanitation workers, transgender persons, persons affected by substance abuse and other marginalized groups, with a focus on inclusive development, skill enhancement and improved access to financial assistance.

This information was given by the Hon'ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Dr. M. Dhanapal in Rajya Sabha.

The Government's flagship scholarship programmes have continued to provide substantial educational support to Scheduled Caste students in Tamil Nadu. Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others, the number of beneficiaries increased from 3,35,642 during 2023-24 to 5,21,123 in 2024-25, before rising further to 5,82,684 in 2025-26. Correspondingly, the Central assistance increased from ₹70.56 crores to ₹109.45 crores and further to ₹121.49 crores over the same period.

Similarly, under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students, the Government supported 9,34,793 students with Central assistance amounting to ₹1,032.09 crores during 2023-24. In 2024-25, scholarships were provided to 6,43,761 students with financial assistance of ₹713.69 crores. The number of beneficiaries increased substantially in 2025-26, with 9,66,840 Scheduled Caste students receiving scholarships supported by ₹1,034.94 crores. Collectively, the two scholarship schemes benefited more than 25.85 lakh Scheduled Caste students in Tamil Nadu over the last three financial years, while Central assistance exceeded ₹3,080 crores, reaffirming the Government's continued emphasis on ensuring equitable access to quality education for Scheduled Caste students.

The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyudaya Yojana (PM-AJAY) has also played an important role in improving socio-economic infrastructure and livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Caste communities across Tamil Nadu. Under the Adarsh Gram component of the scheme, the State received ₹18,606.69 lakh during 2023-24, followed by ₹22,325.63 lakh during 2024-25, while ₹165.55 lakhs have been released so far during 2025-26. The financial support under the Grants-in-Aid component also witnessed sustained assistance, with releases amounting to ₹9,182.94 lakh in 2023-24, ₹9,674.36 lakh in 2024-25, and ₹11,962.81 lakh in 2025-26. Assistance was also extended for hostel infrastructure under the scheme to facilitate better educational opportunities for Scheduled Caste students.

The Government has also continued to prioritize the welfare of senior citizens in Tamil Nadu through dedicated financial assistance under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) and the State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC). Under IPSrC, Central assistance of ₹15.63 crore was released during 2023-24, followed by ₹16.36 crore in 2024-25 and ₹15.78 crore in 2025-26, reflecting the Government's sustained commitment towards strengthening institutional care, health support and welfare services for senior citizens. Under SAPSrC, financial assistance amounted to ₹0.15 crore in 2023-24, while ₹1.43 crore was released during 2025-26 to support State-level initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life of elderly citizens.

The Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM-YASASVI) has continued to expand educational opportunities for students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs). Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship component, the Government released ₹40.47 crore during 2023-24, ₹23.63 crore during 2024-25, and ₹35.29 crore during 2025-26. The financial assistance under the Post-Matric Scholarship component stood at ₹135 crore in 2023-24, ₹119.37 crore in 2024-25, and ₹106.74 crore in 2025-26. The scheme also supported the construction of hostels for OBC boys and girls, with ₹5.25 crore, ₹1.30 crore, and ₹0.03 crore released over the last three financial years respectively.

The Government has also significantly strengthened support for meritorious students through the Top Class Education components of PM-YASASVI. The financial assistance for Top Class Education in Schools increased from ₹1.88 crore in 2023-24 to ₹11.51 crore in 2024-25, before rising substantially to ₹30.62 crore during 2025-26. Similarly, the assistance under the Top Class Education in Colleges component rose from ₹5.71 crore in 2023-24 to ₹14.79 crore in 2024-25, reaching ₹15.41 crore in 2025-26, reflecting the Government's continued efforts to promote access to quality education among socially and educationally disadvantaged communities.

The National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE), launched in 2023 to ensure the safety and dignity of sewer and septic tank workers, has also made notable progress in Tamil Nadu. According to the information placed before the Rajya Sabha, 6,891 sewer and septic tank workers have been validated in the State, with an equal number of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits distributed. The Government has also provided 37 safety devices to Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs), organised 98 workshops on the prevention of hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and extended capital subsidy for mechanised cleaning equipment to 44 sanitation workers. In addition, 34,854 waste pickers have been validated, while 9,925 PPE kits have been distributed among them to improve occupational safety and dignity.

The Central Government reiterated that the Government remains committed to ensuring that the benefits of education, skill development, social protection, rehabilitation and economic empowerment reach every eligible beneficiary across Tamil Nadu. Through sustained investments in scholarships, livelihood promotion, welfare programmes and inclusive development initiatives, the Ministry continues to work towards building an equitable society where vulnerable communities are empowered to participate fully in the nation's social and economic progress.

item.title: Cases Registered Under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Rise to 53,372 in 2023, Convictions and Persons Convicted More Than Double by 2024
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Cases Registered Under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Rise to 53,372 in 2023, Convictions and Persons Convicted More Than Double by 2024 NCRB Data Shows Cases Registered Against Scheduled Castes Rose from 45,995 in 2020 to a Five-Year High of 53,372 in 2023 in 28 States, Persons Convicted Rise from 4,855 to 7,884 in States & UTs Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment today placed before the Rajya Sabha the detailed State/UT-wise statistics on crimes against members of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Cases Registered Under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Rise to 53,372 in 2023, Convictions and Persons Convicted More Than Double by 2024
NCRB Data Shows Cases Registered Against Scheduled Castes Rose from 45,995 in 2020 to a Five-Year High of 53,372 in 2023 in 28 States, Persons Convicted Rise from 4,855 to 7,884 in States & UTs
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment today placed before the Rajya Sabha the detailed State/UT-wise statistics on crimes against members of the Scheduled Castes registered under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, covering the five-year period from 2020 to 2024. The figures are compiled and published by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) in its publication “Crime in India,” the country's official crime-statistics database, whose reports are available up to the year 2024.

This information was given by Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to the Member of Parliament Shri Sanjay Singh in the Rajya Sabha.

The written reply stated that cases registered under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 stood at 45,995 in 2020, of which 36,178 were chargesheeted, 17,113 remained under investigation at the year-end, and 2,613 ended in conviction. Similarly, a total of 61,925 persons were arrested that year, 75,238 were chargesheeted, and 4,855 were convicted, while 177,379 cases remained pending trial at year-end.

In 2021, cases registered held roughly steady at around 45,800 to 46,100, with 37,123 chargesheeted and about 16,300 to 16,400 pending investigation. The convictions rose to 2,848, arrests totalled roughly 58,700 to 58,800, and around 74,000 to 74,100 persons were chargesheeted. The pending trials climbed further to roughly 2,05,800 to 2,06,000, and 5,141 persons were convicted.

The registrations then rose sharply in 2022 to 52,866 cases, with roughly 42,000 to 42,900 chargesheeted and about 17,000 to 17,200 cases pending investigation. The convictions nearly doubled from the previous year to 4,876. The arrests numbered roughly 65,000 to 65,150, persons chargesheeted numbered between 84,074 and 84,145, and persons convicted rose sharply to roughly 9,070 to 9,080. The cases pending trial rose to between 233,500 and 233,750.

In 2023, cases registered rose again to a five-year high of 53,372, with 45,439 chargesheeted and 14,634 pending investigation. The convictions stood at 4,691. The arrests totalled 61,747, persons chargesheeted numbered 90,664 — the highest of the period — and 7,858 persons were convicted. The pending trials climbed to 2, 62,554.

By 2024, cases registered eased to 48,669, with 40,614 chargesheeted and 14,918 pending investigation. The convictions rose to 5,192, the highest figure in the five-year period, and persons convicted reached 10,839, also a five-year high — more than double the 2020 figure. The arrests totalled 55,286 and persons chargesheeted numbered 84,215, while pending trials rose further to 2, 87,694, also the highest of the period.

The Ministry reiterated that the NCRB’s Crime in India report remains the authoritative, publicly available source for tracking crimes against Scheduled Castes, and that the Government continues to monitor category-wise incidents and case outcomes to inform policy on the safety and security of Scheduled Castes communities, the Minister stated.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

As per Entry 18 of List- II (State List) of 7th Schedule of Constitution of India, ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ are State subjects. However, by deriving powers from Entries 6, 7 & 46 of List-III (Concurrent List) of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 [RERA] was enacted by the Parliament to regulate the contractual relationship between homebuyers and promoters.

RERA aims to ensure transparency & accountability in the Real Estate Sector, thereby protecting the interests of the homebuyers.

RERA mandates the registration of real estate projects with the Regulatory Authority before any advertisement, marketing, booking, or sale and in case of contravention of this provision, the promoter is liable to a penalty of up to 10% of the estimated cost of the real estate project, as determined by the Regulatory Authority. Moreover, a Committee was constituted by this Ministry to address challenges during registration of projects across States / Union Territories (UTs) and recommend steps to ensure registration of eligible projects towards effective implementation of RERA. The report of the Committee has been shared with all the Real Estate Regulatory Authorities for further necessary action.

RERA also mandates the promoters to disclose all necessary project details & approvals and deposit 70% of the amounts realized from homebuyers in a separate bank account, which shall be utilized only for land cost and project construction.

RERA also provides for a fast-track dispute resolution mechanism by making the provision of disposal of matter within 60 days. Section 40 of RERA provides for recovery of unpaid interest, penalty or compensation from the promoter as arrears of land revenue and empowers the Adjudicating Officer, Regulatory Authority or Appellate Tribunal to issue necessary orders or directions.

Further, as per Section 41 of RERA, Central Advisory Council (CAC) has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs to advise and recommend the Central Government on all matters concerning the implementation of the Act, including safeguarding the interests of the homebuyers.

Moreover, the Ministry regularly communicates with State Governments on various RERA-related issues, including enhancing the functional and administrative autonomy of Regulatory Authorities and ensuring adequate staff deployment as per operational requirements.

In last one year, the Ministry has held regular consultations with stakeholders including representatives of Homebuyers’ Associations & Real Estate Developers, State Real Estate Regulatory Authorities, among others, for effective implementation of RERA, development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and amendments needed in the Act.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

 

******

SK

item.title: NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi ‘Urban planning’ is a State subject, therefore, the respective State Governments are responsible for planning, initiating and developing proposal for development of urban infrastructure including public transport project, measures to reduce congestion, improve urban mobility through digital technologies etc. in different cities. Central Government has issued various policy guidelines like National Urban Transport Policy 2006 and The Metro Policy 2017…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

‘Urban planning’ is a State subject, therefore, the respective State Governments are responsible for planning, initiating and developing proposal for development of urban infrastructure including public transport project, measures to reduce congestion, improve urban mobility through digital technologies etc. in different cities.

Central Government has issued various policy guidelines like National Urban Transport Policy 2006 and The Metro Policy 2017 for systematic planning and execution of Public Transport project including metro project, which are applicable to all regions of India.

As on date, per se there is no National Smart Public Transport Scheme for integrated public transport, digital ticketing, non- motorized transport, last-mile connectivity.

However, Central Government considers Central Financial Assistance, for deployment of e- buses under various Central Schemes (PM e- Bus Sewa, PM e- Drive etc.) and for implementation of Metro projects as and when posed by concerned State Government. Under above interventions digital ticketing, integrated public Transport etc. are priority items.

National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is an interoperable card with vision of “One Nation, One Card”, which works seamlessly among different Metro/RRTS and Bus operators. The Ministry has issued directions for implementation of National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) ecosystem based on qSPARC (quick Specification for Payment Application of RuPay Chip) developed by National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It is functional in 13 Metro projects and 11 Bus Transport corporations by ensuring ease of ticketing through these digital technologies, which facilitates shift from private vehicle to public transport thereby reducing traffic congestion.

Further, PM-eBus Sewa Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs includes implementation of NCMC based Automatic Fare Collection System (AFCS) for bus operations.

Further, under “Transport Planning and Capacity Building in Urban Transport for metro and non metro projects” sub scheme of MoHUA, various studies like preparation of Integrated Mobility Plan, Detailed Project Reports, Multi Modal integration plans etc. have been eligible components for Central Finance Assistance for cities, ULBs etc. which is considered based on feasibility of proposal as and when posed by concerned State Government.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Railways
item.description: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹220 Crore Electric Traction Upgradation Project on Wadi-Raichur Section of South Central Railway 102 Route Kilometre Wadi-Raichur Section to be Upgraded with 2×25 kV Electric Traction System on High Density Network Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards strengthening railway infrastructure and enhancing capacity on high-density routes, Indian Railways has approved a ₹220 crore project for upgradation of the Electric Traction System from 1×25 kV to 2×25 kV on the Wadi-Raichur section of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves ₹220 Crore Electric Traction Upgradation Project on Wadi-Raichur Section of South Central Railway
102 Route Kilometre Wadi-Raichur Section to be Upgraded with 2×25 kV Electric Traction System on High Density Network
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening railway infrastructure and enhancing capacity on high-density routes, Indian Railways has approved a ₹220 crore project for upgradation of the Electric Traction System from 1×25 kV to 2×25 kV on the Wadi-Raichur section of South Central Railway. The project covers a 102 Route Kilometre (204 Track Kilometre) double-line section and forms part of Indian Railways’ ongoing efforts to modernise traction infrastructure on key rail corridors.

The upgraded traction system will strengthen traction infrastructure and support higher traffic requirements on one of the important sections of the railway network. The Wadi-Raichur section is part of High Density Network (HDN) Route-7 connecting Mumbai-Pune-Wadi-Raichur-Guntakal-Kadapa-Renigunta-Chennai.

The adoption of the 2×25 kV Electric Traction System will strengthen the existing electric traction infrastructure and improve the capability of the section to handle increasing passenger and freight traffic. The upgraded system will enhance operational efficiency while supporting reliable train operations on this strategically important corridor.

The project is aligned with Indian Railways’ ongoing efforts to modernise core infrastructure and strengthen capacity on high-density routes across the network. The approval reflects Indian Railways’ continued commitment to upgrading critical railway infrastructure, improving operational efficiency and developing a modern, reliable and future-ready railway network for passengers and freight customers alike.

*****

Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Vanshita Jaiswal

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Railways
item.description: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹299 Crore Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard Remodelling Project to Enhance Capacity and Passenger Facilities Project to Add 6 New Platforms and 6 Additional Lines While Widening of Existing Six Platforms to Handle Growing Passenger Traffic New East-Side Station Entrance, Electronic Interlocking, Surface Parking and Efficient Circulation Plan to Transform Passenger Experience Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi In a major boost to passenger infrastructure and operational efficiency, Indian Railways has approved the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves ₹299 Crore Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard Remodelling Project to Enhance Capacity and Passenger Facilities
Project to Add 6 New Platforms and 6 Additional Lines While Widening of Existing Six Platforms to Handle Growing Passenger Traffic
New East-Side Station Entrance, Electronic Interlocking, Surface Parking and Efficient Circulation Plan to Transform Passenger Experience
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

In a major boost to passenger infrastructure and operational efficiency, Indian Railways has approved the remodelling of the Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard of South Coast Railway at a cost of ₹299 crore. The project aims to significantly enhance the station's handling capacity, improve punctuality and provide modern passenger amenities at one of the busiest railway terminals in the country.

Comprehensive Remodelling of Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard

The sanctioned project includes comprehensive remodelling of the Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard through construction of additional lines and platforms along with Electronic Interlocking (EI).

Visakhapatnam Railway Station is a major coaching terminal handling nearly 80,000 passengers every day with an average of 113 trains daily. Owing to the existing yard layout, terminating and through trains are required to negotiate surface crossings, leading to detention at approach signals, reduced platform availability and operational constraints.

The yard remodelling will minimise the impact of these surface crossings, reduce detention time, improve platform occupancy and enable handling of additional trains.

Major Capacity Enhancement and Passenger-Centric Infrastructure

The scope of work includes:

  • Dismantling of line loop lines and reorganising the point zones.
  • Widening of the existing six platforms.
  • Construction of six additional platforms equipped with modern passenger amenities.
  • Construction of six additional railway lines.
  • Development of passenger utilities, including ramps, lifts and escalators on the widened platforms to improve accessibility and passenger convenience.
  • Creation of a new entrance on the eastern side of the station along with relocation of the Passenger Reservation System (PRS).
  • Installation of Electronic Interlocking (EI) in the Visakhapatnam station yard along with development of surface parking facilities and an efficient circulating area plan.

Improved Operational Efficiency and Passenger Convenience

The remodelling project will significantly improve operational efficiency by reducing congestion within the coaching yard, increasing platform availability and facilitating smoother movement of trains. The additional infrastructure will enable Visakhapatnam station to handle growing passenger demand while improving punctuality and reducing detention of trains.

 *****

Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj
